# @francofantomius/docs-gen

> Modern, accessible, zero-config Material Design 3 (M3) static documentation generator from Markdown files, powered by Lit, Vite, and @francofantomius/material-components.

`@francofantomius/docs-gen` transforms a directory of Markdown (`.md`) files into an interactive, accessible Material Design 3 Single Page Application (SPA) with instant client-side search, responsive navigation drawer, syntax-highlighted code blocks with copy buttons, GitHub-style callouts, and 16 dynamic M3 color themes. It is distributed both as a reusable GitHub Composite Action for automated deployment to GitHub Pages and as a standalone CLI package (`@francofantomius/docs-gen`).

---

## Guide: How to Implement docs-gen

### 1. Directory Structure

Organize your documentation inside a dedicated folder (default: `docs/`) in your repository:

```text
my-project/
├── docs/
│   ├── docs.config.json         # Optional: site metadata and base URL
│   ├── index.md                 # Required: home landing page (with optional hero)
│   ├── guides/                  # Subdirectory automatically becomes a Category
│   │   ├── getting-started.md
│   │   └── configuration.md
│   ├── components/              # Another category
│   │   ├── button.md
│   │   └── dialog.md
│   └── reference/
│       └── cli.md
├── .github/
│   └── workflows/
│       └── deploy-docs.yml      # Automated GitHub Pages CI/CD workflow
└── package.json                 # Optional: for local npm scripts
```

---

### 2. Method A: GitHub Actions Deployment (Recommended, Zero Local Setup)

To automatically build and deploy documentation to GitHub Pages on every push to `main`, create `.github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml`:

```yaml
name: Deploy Documentation

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: 'pages'
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  deploy:
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout Repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Build Documentation Site
        uses: FrancoFantomius/docs-gen@main
        with:
          docs-dir: 'docs'
          output-dir: '_site'

      - name: Upload GitHub Pages Artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: '_site'

      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
```

#### GitHub Pages Settings
1. Go to your GitHub repository: **Settings** > **Pages**.
2. Under **Build and deployment**, set **Source** to **GitHub Actions**.
3. Push to `main`. The documentation will be built and published at `https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/`.

---

### 3. Method B: Local CLI & NPM Integration

#### Installation
```bash
npm install -D @francofantomius/docs-gen
```

#### Local Development Server (Hot-Reload)
Starts a local Vite dev server that monitors `.md` and `.json` files and refreshes the browser automatically:
```bash
npx docs-gen dev --input docs --port 3000
```

#### Production Build
Compiles all Markdown files, bundles styles and scripts, and exports static assets to the output directory:
```bash
npx docs-gen build --input docs --output _site --base "./"
```

#### NPM Scripts Integration
Add the following commands to your `package.json`:
```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "docs:dev": "docs-gen dev -i docs",
    "docs:build": "docs-gen build -i docs -o _site",
    "docs:preview": "vite preview --outDir _site"
  }
}
```

---

### 4. Configuration Reference (`docs.config.json`)

Place `docs.config.json` inside your docs directory (`docs/docs.config.json`) or specify via `--config`:

```json
{
  "title": "My Project",
  "description": "Material Design 3 documentation for My Project",
  "githubUrl": "https://github.com/my-org/my-project",
  "baseUrl": "./"
}
```

#### Configuration Properties
- `title` (`string`, default: `"Documentation"`): Displayed in the top app bar, drawer header, and browser tab.
- `description` (`string`, default: `"Material Design 3 Documentation"`): Inserted into the `<meta name="description">` tag and search index.
- `githubUrl` (`string`, default: `""`): GitHub repository URL. When provided, a clickable GitHub icon button is rendered in the top app bar.
- `baseUrl` (`string`, default: `"./"`): Base URL path for assets. When deploying to `https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/`, use `"/<repo>/"`. For custom domains, use `"/"` or `"./"`.

#### Precedence Order
Options are resolved in this priority order (highest to lowest):
1. Command-line flags (`--title`, `--base`, `--github`, etc.)
2. Configuration file (`docs.config.json` or path passed to `--config`)
3. GitHub Actions auto-detected environment variables (`github.event.repository.name`, `github.repository`)
4. Built-in defaults

---

### 5. Writing Documentation with Markdown & YAML Frontmatter

Every `.md` file inside your docs directory becomes a page in the documentation site.

#### Frontmatter Schema
Add YAML frontmatter between `---` markers at the very top of each file:

```markdown
---
title: Button Component
category: Components
order: 1
icon: smart_button
badge: <md-button>
description: Interactive button component following Material Design 3 guidelines.
---

# Button Component

Buttons allow users to take actions and make choices with a single tap.
```

#### Frontmatter Fields
| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `string` | First `# Heading` or file name | Page title shown in the top bar, drawer, and search index. |
| `category` | `string` | Parent folder name, or `Overview`/`General` | Category section under which this page appears in the navigation drawer. |
| `order` | `number` | `100` (or `0` for `index.md`) | Sorting order in the drawer. Lower numbers appear first. Prefixing files with digits (e.g. `01-intro.md`) sets order automatically. |
| `icon` | `string` | `menu_book` (`home` for index) | [Material Symbols](https://fonts.google.com/icons) icon name. |
| `badge` | `string` | `""` | Optional chip label displayed next to the title (e.g. `v1.0`, `New`, `<md-button>`). |
| `description` | `string` | `""` | Page summary shown under the heading and indexed in client search. |
| `hero` | `object` | `null` | *(Home page `index.md` only)* Hero banner configuration. |

#### Home Page Hero Banner (`index.md`)
Configure a Material 3 hero card on your landing page:

```markdown
---
title: Docs Gen
category: Overview
order: 0
icon: home
hero:
  badge: "Version 1.0 • Material Design 3"
  title: "Modern Documentation Generator"
  subtitle: "Write documentation in Markdown and deploy clean Material 3 SPAs to GitHub Pages."
  actions:
    - text: "Getting Started"
      link: "#/guides/getting-started"
      variant: "filled"
      icon: "rocket_launch"
    - text: "GitHub"
      link: "https://github.com/my-org/my-project"
      variant: "outlined"
      icon: "code"
---
```
Action `variant` options: `filled`, `outlined`, `tonal`, `text`.

#### GitHub-Style Alert Callouts
Use standard alert callout blockquotes:

```markdown
> [!NOTE]
> Informational callout highlighting useful context.

> [!TIP]
> Helpful recommendations or performance best practices.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Crucial information that users shouldn't miss.

> [!WARNING]
> Warning informing users about potential pitfalls.

> [!CAUTION]
> Warnings regarding critical errors or breaking changes.
```

#### Syntax-Highlighted Code Blocks
Fenced code blocks are converted into `<md-code>` web components with language badges and one-click copy buttons:

````markdown
```javascript
import { buildSite } from '@francofantomius/docs-gen';

await buildSite({ input: 'docs', output: '_site' });
```
````

#### Tables & Custom HTML
- Standard Markdown tables are automatically wrapped in responsive horizontal scroll containers (`table-container` with `api-table`).
- You can embed raw HTML, inline CSS, or interactive Lit Web Components directly in Markdown.

---

### 6. Built-in Features & User Experience

- **Client-Side Search**: Press `/` or `Ctrl + K` (`Cmd + K` on macOS) to instantly focus the `<md-search-bar>`. Searches across page titles, descriptions, categories, and badges with fuzzy matching.
- **Theme Switcher**: Instant switching between Light, Dark, and System modes, persisted in `localStorage`.
- **16 M3 Color Schemes**: Dynamic Material 3 color generation for 16 palettes: Purple (default), Violet, Indigo, Blue, Sky, Cyan, Teal, Green, Light Green, Lime, Yellow, Orange, Deep Orange, Red, Pink, and Slate.
- **Responsive Layout**: Docked navigation drawer on desktop screens; transitions to a modal drawer on mobile viewports.

---

### 7. AI & LLM Integration (`llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`)

`docs-gen` provides native, out-of-the-box support for the [llms.txt standard](https://llmstxt.org):
- **`/llms.txt`**: Automatically generated structured index summarizing all categories, documents, and routes for fast ingestion by AI assistants and crawlers.
- **`/llms-full.txt`**: Complete concatenated markdown containing the full text of all documentation pages in a single plain text file.
- **Custom `llms.txt`**: If a custom `llms.txt` file is placed in your docs input folder (e.g. `docs/llms.txt`), `docs-gen` uses it directly instead of the auto-generated index.

---

## CLI Options Reference

### `docs-gen dev`
| Flag | Short | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--input <path>` | `-i` | `docs` | Source directory containing Markdown files |
| `--port <number>` | `-p` | `3000` | Port for the local development server |
| `--no-open` | | `false` | Disable opening the browser automatically |
| `--title <title>` | `-t` | Inferred | Site title displayed in the app bar |
| `--description <desc>` | `-d` | Inferred | Site description for search and metadata |
| `--github <url>` | `-g` | `""` | GitHub repository link for the top app bar |
| `--config <path>` | `-c` | `<input>/docs.config.json` | Path to custom configuration file |

### `docs-gen build`
| Flag | Short | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--input <path>` | `-i` | `docs` | Source directory containing Markdown files |
| `--output <path>` | `-o` | `_site` | Destination directory for static build output |
| `--base <path>` | `-b` | `./` | Base URL path for assets (e.g. `/<repo>/`) |
| `--title <title>` | `-t` | Inferred | Site title |
| `--description <desc>` | `-d` | Inferred | Site description |
| `--github <url>` | `-g` | `""` | GitHub repository URL |
| `--config <path>` | `-c` | `<input>/docs.config.json` | Path to custom configuration file |

---

## GitHub Action Inputs Reference (`FrancoFantomius/docs-gen@main`)

| Input | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `docs-dir` | No | `'docs'` | Directory containing Markdown documentation |
| `output-dir` | No | `'_site'` | Static output directory ready for Pages upload |
| `base-url` | No | Auto (`/<repo>/`) | Base path for GitHub Pages URL routing |
| `project-title` | No | Auto (Repo Name) | Title rendered in header and top bar |
| `project-description` | No | Auto | SEO meta description |
| `github-url` | No | Auto (Repo URL) | URL for the top app bar GitHub button |
| `config` | No | `''` | Path to custom `docs.config.json` |
